jobDescription: We run a hosted continuous-integration service whose build runners live on six Kubernetes clusters across three cloud regions. The platform team has five engineers and reports to the head of infrastructure. The Platform Engineer upgrades and patches the clusters, maintains the Terraform modules and Helm charts that define them, takes part in the on-call rotation and writes the runbooks the rest of the team relies on. Engineers on this rotation hold cluster-admin access, so the security policy requires them to be CKA certified: the Certified Kubernetes Administrator certification must be current on the start date.
requirements: Upgrades and patches Kubernetes clusters with documented rollback plans.
Maintains Terraform modules and Helm charts for the cluster fleet.
Takes part in an on-call rotation and writes incident runbooks.
Reviews infrastructure changes from other engineers through pull requests.
Holds a current Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) certification.

evidence.text: Infrastructure Engineer, Quorrin DevTools (May 2023 to September 2026): ran minor-version upgrades on four EKS clusters, draining node groups in batches and keeping a written rollback plan for each upgrade window.
Maintained the Terraform modules for VPCs, node groups and IAM roles, and the Helm charts for the ingress controller and the log shipper.
Joined the one-week-in-five on-call rotation from January 2024 and wrote runbooks for disk-pressure evictions and failed certificate renewals.
Reviewed infrastructure pull requests from the team's two other engineers, reading each Terraform plan before approving the merge.

Junior Systems Administrator, Fallowfield Hosting (August 2021 to April 2023): patched Linux virtual machines for shared-hosting customers on a monthly cycle and maintained the Ansible playbooks that configured the web servers.

Work sample attached to the CKA requirement: a score report from a timed practice exam on the Kubelab training simulator, dated 2 August 2026, showing 88 out of 100 across 17 tasks (etcd backup, RBAC, network policies, node troubleshooting) and the simulator's verdict 'exam-ready'.
HR verification note: employment dates for Quorrin DevTools and Fallowfield Hosting were checked against the employment letters supplied by both companies and match the resume.
Reference check summary: the candidate's former team lead at Quorrin confirmed in writing that the candidate ran the EKS upgrade windows and joined the on-call rotation from January 2024.

propositions.text: The candidate ran minor-version upgrades on EKS clusters, draining node groups in batches with a written rollback plan for each upgrade window.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the upgrades and the former team lead confirmed them in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained Terraform modules and Helm charts for the cluster infrastructure.
propositions.rationale: The resume names the modules and charts the candidate maintained.

propositions.text: The candidate holds a current Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) certification.
propositions.rationale: The material offered for the requirement is a practice-exam score from a training simulator; a practice score and a simulator's verdict are not the certification, and the qualification rule forbids calling a candidate certified without explicit cited evidence.

gold.expectedGap: The CKA certification is not established; the work sample is a practice-exam score report from a training simulator.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Describe the practice exam as a practice exam and keep the documented upgrade, Terraform, Helm and on-call work; do not describe the candidate as CKA certified or exam-ready.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has taken the CKA exam, the date of any award and the certificate ID so it can be checked with the issuing body.
